facts.claim: Apr 2026 Substack: Poulos built an AI version of himself from four years of Claude chats (persona markdown files).
facts.quote: People have said some version of “I love how your brain works” to me more times than I can count.

facts.claim: Mar 2025 Substack frames the 'AI knows me better' worry as an autonomy and manipulation question.
facts.quote: Are we truly autonomous decision-makers? Can AI guide us to better choices, or does it subtly manipulate our behavior?

facts.claim: Same post leans on Libet to argue prediction may precede conscious choice (free-will angle).
facts.quote: brain activity predicting a decision occurred several seconds before participants reported consciously making a choice

facts.claim: Jan 2026 Substack: recommendations mean choice starts as a suggestion, not an initiation (paywalled after intro).
facts.quote: Life is no longer something you initiate first. It is something you select from. And that changes what choice actually means.

facts.claim: Jul 2025 Substack (Vox Day) makes the blunt 'it knows before you do' claim; ~55 likes, 19 comments (unlabeled counts).
facts.quote: In many scenarios, SSH-AI will know what you are going to do before you do it.

facts.claim: Jun 2026 Verasight: AI digital twins missed lower-profile poll questions by up to 12.8 points.
facts.quote: On newer or lower-profile questions it was off by as much as 12.8 points, roughly seven times worse.

facts.claim: Same Verasight report: twins matched polls on famous questions (2.1 and 1.8 points off), so they look right where it is easy.
facts.quote: THESEUS came within 2.1 points of a real poll on Trump approval and 1.8 points on the generic ballot.

facts.claim: 2024 Every essay: Dan Shipper simulated his own future journal entries in Claude to test a funding decision.
facts.quote: It allows you to try on a decision like you would a piece of clothing.

facts.claim: 2024 Substack on synthetic respondents: results are mixed and unpredictable in advance (2024, older item).
facts.quote: Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. The bad news is that we don't know in advance which will work.

facts.claim: Latent Space (Substack) interview with Simile CEO cites the 85% self-replication benchmark for 1,000-person agents.
facts.quote: we could replicate people's behaviors and attitudes 85 percent as accurately as people would replicate their own.

facts.claim: Park's critique: frontier LLMs act like rational machines, a bad model of real people.
facts.quote: what these models are really good at today is they're trying to become the super rational, objective machines.

facts.claim: Park's 'say vs do' angle: models learned online self-report, not real-life behavior.
facts.quote: not just what people say they do online, but what they do in real life.

facts.claim: arXiv 2026 (1,305 people, Newcomb-style): many people treat AI as authority on their own behavior.
facts.quote: Over 40% of participants treated AI as such a predictive authority about their own behavior

facts.claim: Same paper: AI predictions alone can steer choices, even narrowing options people consider.
facts.quote: the mere presence of AI predictions may shape their decision-making, narrowing the futures they consider

facts.claim: Oct 2026 'Rigged Draw' Show HN toy (AI guesses your 1-9 picks, scores you vs 206 people): 209 points, 116 comments on mirror page.
facts.quote: After a 10-number warm-up, your final score compares you to 206 people from a psychology study.

facts.claim: Aug 2025 Bulletin essay: the 'prediction is control' angle.
facts.quote: What makes AI prediction both powerful and lucrative is being able to control what happens next.

facts.claim: Nov 2025 Substack: anticipation replaces response as the mode of control.
facts.quote: States and corporations no longer wait to respond to public demand or dissent; they anticipate it.

idea_seeds.title: Beat the Predictor, then Obey It
idea_seeds.one_line: Rigged Draw-style game on shopping choices, then a Newcomb twist: AI shows its guess first, do you comply?
idea_seeds.phone_moment: AI's predicted pick appears face-down, you tap the opposite, and it flips to show it knew (or did not).

idea_seeds.title: What You Say vs What You Do
idea_seeds.one_line: User states a purchase intent, a behavior model predicts from their short action history, gap is shown.
idea_seeds.phone_moment: Two bars side by side: what you said you would buy vs what the model says you will click.

idea_seeds.title: Try On a Decision
idea_seeds.one_line: Enter 5 recent actions, see two simulated next-week futures for a choice, in your own pattern.
idea_seeds.phone_moment: Two future timelines unfold from your last five taps, one per choice.

idea_seeds.title: Famous vs Obscure Twin
idea_seeds.one_line: Twin nails common questions and fails rare ones; let users find where it breaks, with a live error score.
idea_seeds.phone_moment: Slider from common to rare behavior shows prediction confidence collapsing on screen.

viral_evidence.what: Rigged Draw: play-to-be-unpredictable toy vs AI, scored against a study cohort
viral_evidence.mechanic: Personal score vs population benchmark; shareable result; 'can I beat it' challenge

viral_evidence.what: Vox Day 'it will know what you do before you do it' post
viral_evidence.mechanic: Provocative predictability claim; commenters test it on themselves

lessons: Recurring angles: autonomy vs manipulation, prediction is control, say-vs-do gap, twins fail off the famous questions.
Substack engagement on this topic is small (single or low double digits); the viral item found is an interactive toy, not an essay.
Strongest counter-narrative: twins look accurate on easy questions and miss lower-profile ones, so show the failure honestly.
Newcomb-style finding (people defer to AI about themselves) is a fresh, citable provocation for a demo.
gaps: No Substack post found where someone predicted their own purchases or habits with measured results.
No Substack posts found from Astral Codex Ten, One Useful Thing, Experimental History or Understanding AI on this topic.
Substack like and comment counts are unlabeled on fetched pages; treat as approximate.
Joan Westenberg's Algorithmic Personality page returned 404; not used.
Centaur (Nature 2025), Simile funding conflicts, Yui's blog and Pew silicon-sample piece came from search snippets only, not fetched.
Rigged Draw traction was read on a zeli.app mirror, not the HN page itself; the original Show HN was not fetched.
The Latent Space episode year is not shown on the page.
Some fetched quotes were returned by the fetch model and may be paraphrased; code verification is needed.
notes: 24 of 25 tool calls used. Substack coverage is thin; dated items older than 2025 are labeled (2024 Shipper, 10x Insights). Idea seeds are pointers only, not a choice.
